title: Watch: Indian cargo ship engulfed in flames & smoke after projectile strike off Yemen
content: An Indian-flagged cargo vessel was struck by a projectile in Yemeni waters. The ship caught fire and sank off Yemen’s western coast near Hodeidah. All fourteen crew members, including thirteen Indians, were rescued by the Yemeni Coast Guard. The National Resistance Forces blamed Houthi rebels for the unprovoked attack. India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned the incident and called for unimpeded navigation.

title: After Pakistan boxer, Uganda athletes go ‘missing’ in Glasgow after CWG
content: Scottish police are probing reports of athletes from Pakistan and Uganda going missing after the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Four Ugandan boxers reportedly disappeared, with one seeking asylum, while Pakistani boxer Qudratullah was also reported missing. Pakistan finished with just one medal, a bronze for Fatima Zahra, marking its poorest Commonwealth Games campaign in decades.

title: 'Stalker abducted her once': Faridabad teacher lured to gate before her murder
content: A teacher was fatally stabbed by a man who had stalked her for two years.  He had previously abducted her and assaulted her husband, ignoring family assurances.  The victim had warned him of a police complaint if harassment continued.  The accused tricked her to the school gate using her husband's nickname.  Security lapses at the school allowed the masked assailant to enter the campus.

title: Microsoft has 'good news' and 'bad news' for engineers using AI coding tools
content: Microsoft has told engineers to curb AI token spending, with EVP Jay Parikh writing in an internal memo that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for." The company has made OpenAI's cheaper GPT-5.6 the default internal model, set AI token budget targets for every division from July 2026, and given employees dashboards to track individual spend on GitHub Copilot. Some engineers were burning thousands of dollars monthly.

title: Watch: Video captures panic on Air India Phuket-Delhi flight
content: An Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi experienced severe turbulence on Tuesday.  Overhead bins were damaged and debris was scattered across the aisle.  Several passengers and crew members sustained injuries during the turbulent event.  The aircraft briefly lost altitude before landing safely in Delhi.  The Directorate General of Civil Aviation has initiated an investigation into the incident.

title: 'Grave security threat': CJP's Saurav Das alleges media 'breaking into' his house
content: The Cockroach Janta Party began as a satirical online response to a statement by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant but later developed into a broader youth-led campaign. The movement has focused on issues including exam security, administrative reforms and employment-related concerns. Das became one of CJP's most visible representatives due to his background in journalism and his ability to present arguments through data, documents and legal references.

title: US govt may soon increase H-1B and L-1 visas fees for large companies
content: The US government plans to expand an additional fee for certain visa petitions. This fee currently applies to initial H-1B and L-1 visa grants. The proposed change will extend this charge to petitions for extensions of stay. Companies with over fifty employees and a majority on these visas will be affected. This expansion aims to fund biometric entry-exit systems and other government programs.

title: 'When Dhoni stepped away, Kohli-Shastri toughened Indian cricket': Rahane
content: Ajinkya Rahane believes Virat Kohli and Ravi Shastri toughened Indian cricket.  They instilled a fearless and aggressive approach, especially in overseas matches.  India achieved significant success under their leadership during this period.  Rahane expressed concern about the current Test cricket mentality and resilience.  He noted a decline in the patience required for difficult match phases.

title: Inside Naoero’s $90,000 citizenship offer and extra fees
content: Naoero, previously known as Nauru, has introduced a program that offers citizenship to individuals contributing to climate adaptation funding. The initiative focuses on securing finances necessary for relocating vital infrastructure and families further inland, in response to the increasing threats posed by rising sea levels and coastal flooding. Those who successfully navigate the rigorous application process receive a passport, emphasizing the growing trend of seeking second citizenships worldwide.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
content: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.

title: Kanwar Yatra in burqa: SDM court summons Tamanna Malik, husband
content: An SDM court issued notices to Tamanna Malik and her husband Aman Tyagi.  This action followed Malik's announcement to undertake the Kanwar Yatra while wearing a burqa.  Police cited apprehension of a potential breach of peace and law-and-order concerns.  The couple was bound down on personal bonds as a preventive measure.  They must appear before the court to provide an explanation for their decision.

title: In MP, A-certified ‘Dhurandhar’ screened at govt school
content: A video shows an adult film screened for students at a school.  The incident occurred on July thirty-first in Madhya Pradesh's Maihar district.  Villagers lodged a complaint seeking strict action against responsible individuals.  District education officer confirmed an investigation will be conducted soon.  Disciplinary action will follow the inquiry report's findings.

title: 'No trust in judiciary, EC': Dipke on political plans; calls for mass movement
content: Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder, ruled out converting his organization into a political party. He stated public trust in democratic institutions has significantly eroded. Dipke emphasized the urgent need for a nationwide people's movement and public pressure. This movement aims to restore accountability and neutrality in key institutions. The CJP will continue functioning as a pressure group focusing on various national issues.

title: Nearly half of India's workforce wants a new job. Here's why
content: Google leads India's most attractive employer brands, with Tata Group and Amazon following closely.  Nearly half of India's workforce plans job changes within the next six months.  Work-life balance and career progression are key factors influencing employee preferences.  Employers must adapt to evolving talent expectations beyond conventional benefits.  Organisations offering growth and flexibility will attract and retain top talent effectively.

content: With Kenny Pickett stepping up as the Carolina Panthers’ new starting quarterback, he navigates the storm of social media criticism regarding his hand size. Just before the Hall of Fame game, he prepares to showcase his skills while previous starter Bryce Young watches on. A strong performance could solidify Pickett’s position as the team’s long-term solution at quarterback.

title: 'Blast, blast' budget turned out 'waste, waste': Stalin's 'reel CM' swipe at Vijay
content: Tamil Nadu's opposition leader M.K. Stalin criticized the TVK government's budget as a waste. He stated the budget repackaged old schemes and lacked new vision. The finance minister presented a budget aiming for a $1.5 trillion economy by 2031. Opposition parties also pointed out unfulfilled election promises and debt concerns. The budget included allocations for schools, higher education, and welfare initiatives.

title: 'Why no system to remove defamatory posts?' Bombay HC on Gadkari deepfake case
content: The Bombay High Court ordered social media intermediaries to remove vile and abusive online content.  These posts falsely linked Union Minister Nitin Gadkari to the ethanol-blended petrol controversy.  The court granted urgent interim relief to the minister against several platforms.  Gadkari sought damages for fabricated and defamatory digital content, including deepfake videos.  The court also directed intermediaries to furnish basic customer information of content creators.

title: Watch: Valet drives car into parking lift shaft, plunges 2 floors
content: A car fell about twenty-five feet down a parking lift shaft. The incident occurred at the Horizon Gold building in Kandivli West. A valet attendant was steering the vehicle out of the building at the owner's request. The attendant was extricated by onlookers and taken to a local hospital. He sustained injuries after the unexpected fall into the shaft.

title: J'khand student leader takes water after Wangchuk's appeal, to continue hunger strike
content: After four days without food or water, Jharkhand student leader Devendra Nath Mahto drank water following an appeal from climate activist Sonam Wangchuk but said his indefinite fast over alleged irregularities in state recruitment examinations would continue.

title: Every fish tested in Yamuna carried microplastics. What it means for your dinner plate
content: Scientists discovered microplastics in every fish species sampled from the Yamuna River.  Fish from Delhi's stretch showed much higher contamination than those from upstream Haryana.  These plastic particles were found not only in digestive tracts but also in muscle tissues.  This contamination indicates a widespread issue within the river's aquatic food chain.  Addressing this requires reducing microplastic pollution from various sources.

title: Wanted on Red Notice, CBI brings back fraud accused Vishakha Rathod from UAE
content: Vishakha Rathod, a suspect in a financial fraud case, was deported from the UAE.  She was apprehended by Maharashtra Police upon her arrival at Pune Airport.  This successful operation highlights India's commitment to bringing fugitives back home.  Law enforcement agencies located seventy-one wanted fugitives abroad in the past year.  This marks the highest number of overseas traces recorded in twelve years.

title: What is Chandipura virus? Doctor explains how it spreads
content: Gujarat is grappling with a new outbreak of the Chandipura virus, which has been linked to several suspected child fatalities. This virus is known to trigger acute encephalitis, which can escalate quickly. Initially, it presents with symptoms similar to common fevers, but any neurological signs necessitate immediate medical attention. It's spread by infected sandflies and mosquitoes, so preventing bites and maintaining hygiene is essential for safety.

title: India to get its first plastic notes next year: RBI governor shares timeline
content: The government has authorised the Reserve Bank of India to print up to 2 billion polymer (plastic) notes - 1 billion each in the Rs 10 and Rs 20 denominations for field trials. At present, there is no proposal to replace paper currency entirely.

title: Railways ordered to pay family Rs 2 lakh after protest disrupted Amritsar trip
content: A consumer commission upheld a district forum's order for Railways to pay Rs 2 lakh compensation.  The family's Amritsar trip was disrupted after train services were suspended due to a protest.  Passengers were not properly informed or assisted after the train halted for hours.  The commission found this omission constituted a deficiency in service by the Railways.  The Railways' appeal was dismissed, confirming the compensation amount awarded.

title: AICF confirms new dates for chess nationals after GM Abhijeet flags 2026 snub
content: The All India Chess Federation has rescheduled the senior National Chess Championship to November 29-December 9, 2026, in Varanasi, after GM Abhijeet Gupta objected to its proposed March 2027 dates. AICF held discussions with stakeholders to come up with a solution while retaining the venue. Gupta had cited school board exams and the risk of effectively losing the 2026 edition.

title: India's services PMI hits over 4.5-year low as demand, new orders lose momentum
content: India's services sector growth slowed significantly in July, reaching its weakest pace in over four years. New business inflows expanded at the slowest rate since early 2022, driven by softer demand. Overseas demand remained relatively resilient, with export business outperforming overall sales growth. Employment growth improved modestly, while business confidence weakened to a seven-month low. Input cost inflation eased, and companies raised selling prices at the fastest pace since April.

title: Rock, paper, scissors & millionaire: Aus Open's Million-Dollar 1 Point Slam
content: The eagerly anticipated Australian Open is set to reintroduce the exciting Million-Dollar 1 Point Slam event in 2027. This thrilling exhibition match allows players to compete for a staggering prize of one million Australian dollars. After a successful inaugural run where an amateur triumphed, fans are looking forward to witnessing more suspenseful moments as one single point determines the fate of each match.

title: Can a registered rent agreement be changed? Here's what the law says
content: In India, rent agreements can be altered legally once registered, provided both parties agree. For small adjustments, simple written addendums referring back to the original document are sufficient. However, significant changes may require drafting a new rent agreement altogether. It's essential to register any tenancy agreements lasting longer than twelve months. Written contracts help ensure stability and allow for necessary adjustments in the future.

title: TN SSLC supplementary result 2026 out: Download Class 10 marks memo
content: The Directorate of Government Examinations has announced the SSLC supplementary results for 2026 today. Students can now access their provisional marks memos on the official DGE Tamil Nadu website. These supplementary exams were conducted for students who needed to clear additional subjects. Applications for scanned answer scripts will be accepted on August 10 and 11. The fee for a scanned copy of an answer script is Rs 275 per subject.

The reshuffle occurs amid heightened political activity and internal party discussions.

content: According to official estimates, the Rs 2,000 threshold would cover only around 5% of all UPI transactions, although these account for nearly 65% of the total value processed on the platform. As a result, routine purchases such as milk, vegetables, groceries, or payments for auto-rickshaws and taxis are unlikely to be affected. UPI processed 23.7 billion transactions worth Rs 29.9 lakh crore in July.

content: Asked about the discrepancy between his latest explanation and the one he gave on Monday, Satheesan declined to respond. He also refused to disclose the identity of the investor

title: ‘Don’t hide, answer in Parliament’: Opposition MPs slam Amit Shah, take out protest march in Parliament complex
content: They are disrespecting Parliament. It has been so many days but they don't want to step inside the House, says Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge

title: Congress says E20 hurt middle class, favoured ethanol producers
content: The Modi Government's Transport Minister (Nitin Gadkari) had claimed that ethanol blending would bring diesel costs down to Rs. 50 per litre and provide a petrol alternative at Rs. 55 per litre. No such reduction has materialised, says Congress leader Jairam Ramesh

title: Terrorist hideout unearthed in J&K’s Poonch
content: Two magazines of an AK assault rifle along with 117 rounds of ammunition and 17 rounds of 9-mm pistol ammunition were seized from the hideout, the officials said

title: Chargesheet filed in actor Dileep’s media trial case, Kerala govt informs HC
content: State tells High Court that probe in all five cases against a TV channel for allegedly violating a gag order in the actor assault case of 2017 has been completed. The court was considering a petition by actor Dileep

title: Maharashtra govt. bans analogue paneer for one year, cites food safety norm violations
content: Offenders could face life imprisonment and a fine of up to ₹10 lakh, as per a recent government order

title: Kerala faces deadly landslides amid intensifying monsoon rains | Explained
content: Kerala receives around 3,000 mm of annual rainfall, often in uneven, high-intensity spells that are becoming more frequent and extreme, exacerbated by global warming and climate change

title: Kerala rain havoc: Govt announces ₹8-lakh aid for kin of each deceased
content: Death toll from rain-related incidents rises to 26; four still missing, says Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan

title: Channi’s options shrink as Congress refuses to budge in Punjab
content: Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi finds himself in a difficult position after locking horns with the party leadership over the recent organisation overhaul

title: Baghel asks workers to beware of ‘traitors’ within Punjab Congress
content: Addressing the gathering in Bathinda, he said the next elections will not be fought by the candidates alone, but by the entire party’s rank and file, underlining the need for strengthening the organisation at the grassroots level

title: Punjab Congress kicks off mass mobilisation programme ahead of Assembly polls
content: Congress’s general secretary in charge for Punjab, Bhupesh Bhagel said the ruling AAP was on the way out; the Congress was the only option for the State, even as he predicted a five-cornered contest in Punjab this time

title: Tamil Nadu Budget: Lean-period fishing assistance raised to ₹7,000 per family
content: Under the ‘Vetri Magalir Goat Rearing Scheme’, five goats or sheep will be provided with a 100% subsidy to destitute widows, deserted women, transgender persons, and PwDs living in rural areas

title: As Ganeshotsav nears, the PoP idol battle drags on in Bombay HC
content: Over the past two years, the Bombay High Court has heard multiple petitions seeking restrictions on immersion of PoP Ganesh idols in natural water bodies; the matter remains pending with interim orders issued for the upcoming Ganeshotsav festival
